{{Short description|Combination of higher category theory with Chern–Simons theory}}
In [[mathematics]], '''∞-Chern–Simons theory''' (not to be confused with [[infinite-dimensional Chern–Simons theory]]) is a generalized formulation of [[Chern–Simons theory]] from [[differential geometry]] using the formalism of [[higher category theory]], which in particular studies [[∞-categories]]. It is obtained by taking [[General abstract nonsense|general abstract]] analogs of all involved concepts defined in any cohesive [[∞-topos]], for example that of smooth [[∞-groupoid|∞-groupoids]]. [[Principal bundle|Principal bundles]] on which [[Lie group|Lie groups]] act are for example replaced by ∞-principal bundles on with [[Group object|group objects]] in ∞-topoi act.<ref>Definition in Schreiber 2013, 1.2.6.5.2</ref> The theory is named after [[:de:Shiing-Shen_Chern|Shiing-Shen Chern]] and [[Jim Simons|James Simons]], who first described [[Chern–Simons form|Chern–Simons forms]] in 1974,<ref name=":18">{{cite journal |last1=Chern |first1=Shiing-Shen |author-link1=Shiing-Shen Chern |last2=Simons |first2=James |author-link2=Jim Simons |date=September 1996 |title=Characteristic forms and geometric invariants |journal=World Scientific Series in 20th Century Mathematics |language=en |volume=4 |pages=363–384 |doi=10.1142/9789812812834_0026|isbn=978-981-02-2385-4 }}</ref> although the generalization was not developed by them.
